name: High Frequency: Short Wavelength
description: Set frequency to maximum (1.0). Higher frequency = shorter wavelength = more interference fringes packed into the same angular range. This directly demonstrates the wave equation relationship: lambda * f = c (constant wave speed).

successCriteria.description: Observe very dense interference fringes at high frequency
Compare high freq (1.0) vs low freq (0.2): count how fringe count scales with frequency

hints.message: High frequency = short wavelength = many fringes. The wave speed c is fixed, so lambda decreases as frequency increases.
This is why blue light (high frequency) produces finer interference patterns than red light (low frequency) in optical double-slit experiments.
